question.text: What is the FUNDAMENTAL difference between a Non-Profit Organisation (NPO) and a For-Profit Social Enterprise (FPE) as per the chapter?

answer.text: NPOs are tax exempt while FPEs pay corporate tax — profitability alone differentiates them
NPOs rely on donations and grants for funding while FPEs generate their own revenue for financial sustainability, though FPE profits are typically ploughed back
NPOs must register on SSE while FPEs cannot register on SSE
FPEs are ineligible to receive CSR funding while NPOs are the only CSR-eligible recipients

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.3 the fundamental difference is the SOURCE of funding — NPOs rely on donations/grants, while FPEs generate revenue through sale of goods or services. FPEs can still be SEs if profits are reinvested for social purpose. Both can list on SSE. The Trap: Option A is reductive — tax treatment is a consequence, not the definitional difference. Option C is factually wrong (both NPOs and FPEs can list on SSE). Option D is wrong — CSR under Section 135 flows to both NPOs and eligible FPEs. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) where both NPO and FPE recommendations differ, and to Ch 10 (Taxation) where 80G and Section 11 apply differently to NPOs vs FPEs. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When scoping evidence, treat NPO engagements as 'grant utilisation + output focus' and FPE engagements as 'revenue-to-impact ratio' focus. Your sampling plan (SAS-200/400/500) must pivot on this difference.
